I can do this, but I need one explicit confirmation before I perform any destructive changes.

Planned judgement and criteria (what I will treat as an “old draft”):
- Files in the Docs folder named or containing “draft”, “DRAFT”, “v2”, “v3”, “v4”, or similar draft markers in the title; OR
- Files not marked as drafts but whose last-modified date is >12 months old; OR
- Exact duplicates (same content) where one copy is clearly newer — I’ll keep the newest and archive/delete the duplicates.

Recommended safe default (what I suggest doing):
- Move identified old drafts into a new subfolder Employee handbook/Archive (creates it if needed). This preserves content and is reversible.

Destructive alternative (only if you explicitly allow it):
- Permanently delete the identified old drafts from Docs (irreversible).

Please reply with exactly one of these options:
1) "Move to Archive" — go ahead and move matching files to Employee handbook/Archive (recommended, reversible). 
2) "Permanently delete" — permanently delete the matching files (irreversible). 

If you prefer different criteria (e.g., shorter/longer age threshold), say so in the same reply; otherwise I’ll use the criteria above. I will not proceed until you choose option 1 or 2.
